what: Every check in Shay Green's spc_smp cartridge that reached a verdict, and what each one said. The values a console produced are read out of his own uploaded programs; the values here are read out of this unit's memory.
why: His harness reports only the first failure and then restarts, so one disagreement hides every check after it. The run records the verdict and then turns that check's four conditional branches into no-ops so it carries on. Nothing rewrites what a check expects: a verdict is ignored, never changed.
producedBy: A cut-down console driving the cartridge into this unit: a 65816 from mos65xx-python, the cartridge decoded as LoROM, $2140-$2143 wired to the unit's four ports, and the four-byte comparison against $dc to $df every check ends with turned into no-ops after its verdict is recorded. It is not carried here, for the reason given under what is deliberately not modelled. What is carried is this record, so the verdicts can be disputed without rebuilding the harness.
evidence: All eighteen verdicts agree with values taken on a console, including the three random timer checks and the memory access check, which agree since the timers share one free-running prescaler and match the divider by equality.
howToSettleIt: Settled for what the cartridge reaches. The nineteenth check, CPU Timing/time all opcodes, prints its name and reaches no comparison here.
